questions.question:
A pod called `app-xyz` has been created in the `orion` namespace. It uses a secret as environment variables.

1. Extract the decoded value of the `CONNECTOR_PASSWORD` key from the Secret and save it to the file `/tmp/exam/secrets/CONNECTOR_PASSWORD` on `cks9999`.
2. Then recreate the pod so that instead of using the secret as an environment variable, the secret is mounted as a **read-only** volume at the path `/mnt/connector/password` for the application to use.

You may delete and recreate the pod.

verification.description: File /tmp/exam/secrets/CONNECTOR_PASSWORD contains the decoded CONNECTOR_PASSWORD value
Pod app-xyz mounts the secret read-only at /mnt/connector/password (and no longer sets it as an env var)
Pod app-xyz is Ready

questions.question:
A pod called `redis-backend` exists in the `prod-x12cs` namespace and is exposed as a `ClusterIP` service on port `6379`.

Using a NetworkPolicy called `allow-redis-access` in the `prod-x12cs` namespace, lock down incoming connections to this pod to only:

1. Any pod in the same namespace with the label `backend=prod-x12cs`
2. All pods in the `prod-yx13cs` namespace (its namespace carries the label `access=redis` - use a namespaceSelector with the existing label)

All other incoming connections must be blocked. Select the pod with its existing label `run=redis-backend` and restrict traffic to TCP port `6379`.

verification.description: NetworkPolicy allow-redis-access selects run=redis-backend and declares policy type Ingress
Ingress allows pods in the same namespace labeled backend=prod-x12cs
Ingress allows the prod-yx13cs namespace via namespaceSelector access=redis
Ingress restricted to TCP port 6379

questions.question:
A pod called `apps-cluster-dash` in the `gamma` namespace was created with the service account `cluster-view`, which has cluster-wide view permissions. The secret token is still mounted into the pod.

Secure the pod so that the service account secret token is **no longer mounted** into it. You may delete and recreate the pod. Keep using the `cluster-view` service account.

verification.description: Pod apps-cluster-dash sets automountServiceAccountToken: false
No service account token volume/volumeMount remains in the pod
Pod apps-cluster-dash is Ready

questions.question:
A developer called `martin` needs access to work on the `dev-a`, `dev-b` and `dev-z` namespaces:

- In `dev-a` and `dev-b` he can perform **any** operation on any pod (this is already correct)
- In `dev-z` he must only be allowed to `get` and `list` pods

The current setup in `dev-z` is too permissive. Fix the Role called `dev-user-access` in the `dev-z` namespace so it only grants `get` and `list` on pods. Do not change the roles in `dev-a` or `dev-b`, and keep the same role name.

verification.description: Role dev-user-access in dev-z grants only get and list on pods
Roles in dev-a and dev-b are unchanged (full pod access for martin)
RoleBindings still bind dev-user-access to martin in all three namespaces
martin can no longer create pods in dev-z but still can in dev-a

questions.question:
In the `dev` namespace (create it if needed), create the following resources:

1. A Role called `dev-write` granting `get`, `watch`, `list` and `create` on pods in the same namespace
2. A ServiceAccount called `developer`
3. A RoleBinding called `dev-write-binding` that binds the `dev-write` role to the `developer` ServiceAccount
4. A pod using the template provided at `/tmp/exam/dev-pod.yaml`. The pod must run with the `developer` service account (update the template as necessary before creating it).

verification.description: Role dev-write grants get,watch,list,create on pods in dev
ServiceAccount developer and RoleBinding dev-write-binding exist and are correctly linked
Pod from the template runs with serviceAccountName developer
The developer ServiceAccount can create pods in dev

questions.question:
Pods have been created in the `alpha` namespace. Delete every pod that is **not immutable**.

A pod counts as immutable when its container sets `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`. Remember the default when the field is not present.

verification.description: Immutable pod solaris (readOnlyRootFilesystem: true) still exists
Mutable pod sonata (readOnlyRootFilesystem: false) was deleted
Pod triton (field absent, defaults to mutable) was deleted

questions.question:
A pod called `frontend-site` has been created in the `omni` namespace with more permissions than it needs. Several service accounts exist in the namespace (`fe`, `frontend`, `frontend-default`, plus `default`).

Apply the principle of least privilege:

1. Recreate the pod `frontend-site` using the service account with the **minimum privileges** (excluding the `default` service account - inspect the RoleBindings to find which service account has no permissions).
2. Once the pod runs under the correct service account, delete the other unused service accounts in `omni` (excluding `default` and the one you selected).

verification.description: Pod frontend-site runs under the least-privilege service account frontend-default
Unused service accounts fe and frontend are deleted
frontend-default still exists and the pod is Ready

questions.question:
A pod called `busy-rx100` has been created in the `production` namespace. Secure the pod by recreating it with the RuntimeClass called `gvisor`. You may delete and recreate the pod.

Note: the gvisor runtime itself is not installed in this cluster - the pod may not start. What matters is that the pod is correctly configured.

verification.description: Pod busy-rx100 sets runtimeClassName: gvisor
Pod busy-rx100 still exists in production with image nginx and label run=busy-rx100
